### Observed differences

- The clearest difference concerns the segment between A36 and A21. In the earlier window, A36 was always followed by exactly one of three activities — A14, A15 or A20 (about 35, 35 and 30 in 100 of A36's outgoing transitions) — and each of those three was always followed directly by A21. In the later window, A36 is followed directly by A21 in all transitions, and A14, A15 and A20 are not observed at all. [DIR027, DIR010, DIR011, DIR016]
- Participation in A14, A15 and A20 fell from about 35, 30 and 35 in 100 traces to 0 of 200 traces; their position distributions vanish, and A21's typical position moves slightly earlier (median about 0.38 to 0.36 of the trace length). [OCC013, OCC014, OCC019, POS001, POS002, POS004, POS005]
- Relations change accordingly: pairs among A14, A15 and A20 move from "exactly one of the two occurs" (about 30–35 in 100 traces) to "neither occurs" in all 200 later traces, and their co-occurrence with A21, A26 and A36 drops to zero. [REL001, REL003, REL008, REL004, REL009, REL016]
- The distance from A36 to A21 collapses from always two steps to always one step, so the three activities were bypassed rather than reordered. [LAG002]
- Away from this segment, routing after A19 shifted toward A26 (about 41 to 60 in 100 of A19's outgoing transitions, with A16 down from about 31 to 16 in 100); A10 and A11 repeat slightly more often (about 1.4 to 1.5 executions per trace, recurrence in about 27 to 32 in 100 traces) and A12 appears in more traces (about 21 to 29 in 100). [DIR015, LAG001, OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, DIR009]
- Several broader shifts of moderate size appear: A01 and A03–A05 each drop from about 58 to about 50 in 100 traces while A02 and A06–A08 rise to about 50; A21, A28 and A29 shift their route shares by about 8 points; A30 and A31 lead more often to A27 (about 38 to 49 in 100). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC006, OCC007, DIR017, DIR020, DIR022]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the three-way branch between A36 and A21 — in which every trace executed A36, then exactly one of A14, A15 or A20, then A21 — is no longer executed in the later window: A36 now leads directly to A21, and A14, A15 and A20 were not observed in any of the 200 later traces after appearing in 60–70 of 200 before. This is shown directly by A36's successor profile (before: only A14/A15/A20; after: only A21) and by the A36→A21 distance changing from always two steps to always one; the participation, position and relation items on the same activities all point the same way, and the drops to 0 of 200 traces are larger than what arises in roughly 995 of 1,000 random re-splits of the pooled data. [DIR027, LAG002, OCC013, OCC014, OCC019, POS001, POS002, POS004, REL004, REL009, REL016]

Limitations: zero participation strictly establishes only that A14, A15 and A20 were not observed in the later window, and the many occurrence, position and relation items on these three activities describe one underlying change rather than independent confirmations; no chance-expectation baseline for the number of qualifying items is included in the evidence, so the judgement rests on the directness and consistency of the successor, lag and positional evidence. The competing explanation that the later window sampled only traces of a variant that never contains A14, A15 or A20 cannot be fully excluded, although a fall from 60–70 of 200 traces to 0 of 200 is difficult to attribute to sampling alone. [OCC013, OCC014, OCC019]

Other differences: routing after A19 now favours A26 over A16; A10 and A11 repeat slightly more often and A12 participates more; and several moderate share shifts exist among the early alternatives A01–A08, around A21/A28/A29, and from A30/A31 toward A27. These are consistent with existing paths being taken with different frequencies, but they are not part of the main hypothesis. [DIR015, LAG001, OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, OCC001, OCC002, OCC006, DIR017, DIR022]
